item.title: Warm Winters Are Breaking the Ski Industry — and Artificial Snow Isn’t Enough
item.description: The ski industry is racing to fight the impacts of climate change mainly with snowmaking. But the irony is hard to ignore: the very systems keeping many slopes open also burn energy and emit greenhouse gases.

item.title: What a Chaotic Social Network for AI Agents Reveals About the Future of Booking
item.description: AI agents are talking to each other on the Moltbook social network — no humans required. Soon, they’ll be booking travel too.

item.title: India’s Travel Budget: Small Marketing Spend, a Tax Win, Infrastructure Push
item.description: The Union Budget’s impact depends largely on where you sit in the travel value chain. For inbound-focused businesses, there is little to celebrate amid muted promotion spends. For outbound players, however, tax relief offers a clear and immediate boost.

item.title: Indian Hotels Face a New Competitor: The Food Delivery App
item.description: F&B is a major revenue driver for hotels. But it is likely that the boom from banqueting is overshadowing how room guests are no longer willing to pay through their nose when options are just a click away.

item.title: United’s Scott Kirby Warns AI ‘Tells You What You Want to Hear’
item.description: Kirby's framework — AI for optimization, humans for judgment — is more specific than what most travel executives have articulated. It's worth paying attention to.

item.title: America’s Low-Cost Airline Playbook Is Broken. Here’s What the Next Model Looks Like.
item.description: The U.S. has become the hardest place in the world to run a ULCC, and only highly focused models are surviving.

item.title: Google’s Latest AI Search Features Look Like a Personalized Travel Concierge
item.description: Google is stitching its AI search features into a single workflow. For some users, that means a smarter, more personalized experience, with AI that shapes responses based on real travel preferences without leaving search.

item.title: India Moves to Cut Aircraft Parts Duties as It Pushes to Build Planes at Home
item.description: While aircraft manufacturing in India may still be some way off, but the government is already taking steps to make domestic production commercially viable.

item.title: JTB CEO Says Japan’s Tourism Problem Is Distribution, Not Overtourism
item.description: Japan doesn’t have too many tourists. It has too many tourists being sent to the same places. Until that changes, talks on solving overtourism will just remain recycled rhetoric.

item.title: Uber Rebuilds Asia Presence Starting Small in Macau
item.description: With the Macau entry, Uber is making its way back into Asia. But it is moving slowly. And this time, it is sticking to the rules.
